Done. Narrow handoff complete.

## What raced (`race.8310`)

`mcpE2EChild` wired the child's `cmd.Stderr` to a plain `bytes.Buffer`. `os/exec` drains that buffer from its own `io.Copy` goroutine for the child's whole lifetime, while the harness reads the same buffer via `c.stderr.String()` on every `send`/`await`/`finish` to enrich failure messages. `send`'s eager error-arg evaluation (`require.NoError(t, err, "...: %s", c.stderr.String())`) put a `String()` read (line 151) in flight against `io.Copy`'s `grow` write — an unsynchronized `bytes.Buffer`, which is the exact detector finding.

## Fix (in-scope only)

- Added **`syncBuffer`** to `test/e2e/mcp_e2e_test.go`: one mutex over one embedded `bytes.Buffer`, exposing **only** `Write` (satisfies `cmd.Stderr`) and `String` (assertions). No `bytes.Buffer` method promoted → no unlocked path. Field `stderr` changed `*bytes.Buffer` → `*syncBuffer`.
- Detector not suppressed, no diagnostics dropped, no child-wait added, protocol assertions/bounds untouched — per the brief's constraints.
- **Stdout/close audit:** the only memory-level race was stderr. `finish`'s `cmd.Wait()` overlapping the live stdout scanner is the documented `StdoutPipe` caveat but fd-poller-safe (not a data race); returned to main as optional hardening.

## Validation (and honest limits)

- gofumpt (pinned) on both files: clean.
- New `test/e2e/mcp_stderr_capture_test.go` → `TestSyncBufferConcurrentWriterReader` drives the exact writer/reader shape (1 `io.Copy` writer vs 8 `String()` readers). **PASS under `-race` on Windows**, recorded via `run.py` id `mcp-harness-syncbuffer-race-20260922`. Compiling it built the whole `test/e2e` package under `-race`, confirming the type change breaks nothing.
- **Limit:** I did not reproduce the end-to-end failure. **Main must re-run `TestStdioServerEndToEnd` + suite in a fresh overlay** (not the immutable `/work/linux-readers-20260922-1422`) under the product-child lane to confirm `race.8310` is gone in situ.

Report: `plans/sdd/V6-remediation/mcp-harness-race-resolution.md`. No source outside the two in-scope files was edited.
